card.name: Bizhu
card.tagline: Chakma New Year dance ushering out the old year
card.profile: Bizhu (also Bizu/Bijhu) is the most popular dance of the Chakma people, performed during their three-day Bizu New Year festival around 12-14 April, marking Chaitra-Sankranti, the last day of the Bengali calendar (Wikipedia; Tripura State Portal). The dance climaxes the second day, Mul Bizhu, and is thought to have originated as a devotional offering performed within Chakma temple precincts; it is a group dance with participants aligned in square or circular patterns and is marked by abrupt pauses (Wikipedia). It is accompanied by flutes and drums including the dhol, baajhi, kheng-garang and dhuduk; women wear flowers and silver ornaments (Wikipedia; Tripura State Portal).
card.insight: Originally rooted in jhum (shifting) cultivation as a propitiation of the earth for a good harvest, Bizhu has in recent decades lost some agrarian linkages and become primarily a social celebration of Chakma identity (Wikipedia).
